chars.summary: Chars lens verification of the fix wave at d582d21. Fully fixed: the Thug's half-face (chars-01) and his skin now bruises on both cheeks; the Thug's chest scribble (chars-02), with the V-shaped hood drape and the pocket ink kept; the Thug's waistband dashes (chars-08); the Kicker's mask slashes (chars-05); the Bruiser's double visor stripes and cream wedge (chars-06, colour part); the Punk's vest. The veteran is still clearly different at 5 m. The Ox claim (a) holds. His face faces are slot 7, and their texel codes are 97.6% slot 7 with no slot 53. Swatches on and off look the same, and bloodied, the face takes the skin bruise. So the mauve patches are the toon shadow band, and the face stays flat: answered, not fixed. Four defects stay or are new. (1) The Kicker's eye fix shipped the build its own call rejected. The region max z in pipeline.json is 1.685 (the call says 1.665), so the cap's brim tips and underside are painted skin, and the face is a blank pale band, further from the concept's shaded eyes. (2) The Bruiser's helmet still bleeds on a front band just above the visor: 64 slot-44 faces at z 1.64-1.71 sit below helmet_top's min z of 1.71, and a red drip lands there at 20% health. (3) Ox's new face ink is a hairy blot under the nose plus a stray comma at the jaw at 1 m, over the remaining mauve patches. (4) The Bruiser's under-visor scarf keeps the stair-stepped outline, now purple on grey. No new crawl was visible in the fight sheet, though that check was coarse.

world.summary: The fixes hold, but the wave added one new visible defect. On the hurt cue (feedback-world-01 and -03), every recorded hit lights the edge on the attacker's side. That covers 41 hits in the hurt acts and the real hits in passive_mix and passive_six whose side I could pin down. The new finisher, blocked and burst acts exist and read correctly. The boss roof gap toggle (feedback-world-02 and code-02) is gone: tour pose 17 d1 went from 0.213 (jitter 0.138) to 0.053 (jitter 0.011), and the other 19 poses are unchanged. The ground (feedback-world-05) is paler and calmer, and its higher A1 numbers come from bold, clean features, not shimmer. The new defect: the InsetBlock recesses leave 2 to 4 cm steps where a pulled-back face extends past its partner, and the edge pass now draws ink seam lines there. I found them on the catwalk brick wall, the terrace door pillars, the side of the penthouse, a pilaster at the street start and a building corner in the skyline-up view. At distance they are dashed and crawl slightly. Second, the new bearing uses the camera's full pitched basis against the attacker's feet. Beyond about 30 degrees of pitch, front and back swap, for example a rear hit shows as a frontal one while the player looks down to stomp. Two lows remain: the street's mirror pair is visible down its length, and the rooms' coplanar guard was relaxed to 0.5 m2.

findings.title: Kicker at 1-1.6 m: the merged eyes region is the build FIX-ART-A rejected (z max 1.685, not 1.665). The cap's brim tips and underside turn skin, and the face is a blank pale band with no cap shade.
findings.detail: chars-04 is PARTLY FIXED. The black bar and its scratches are gone, and the band now bruises as skin. However, assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json has the 'eyes' region max z at 1.685 (line 434) and the 'eyes' zone max z at 1.69. FIX-ART-A A-4 says the final values are 1.665 and 1.675, and that 1.685 'cut 2 cm off the cap's lower edge and made it read short'. The shipped export matches 1.685 (run.py --check YES), so the rejected first build is what merged. At 1 m and 60/120 degrees, a skin-coloured lip sticks out of the brim's left tip. In profile (dk yaw90), the brim's underside is skin. Against the concept (kicker_c.jpg: dark shade under the brim with eyes in it), the result moves further away at 2.2 m: before it read as sunglasses, now it reads as an empty pale strip between the cap and the mask, a featureless face (Game-boy's 'blobby' ask).

findings.suggested_fix: assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json: set the eyes region max z to 1.665 and the eyes zone max z to 1.675, as the call says, then rebuild and check the brim at yaw 0/90. For the concept's shaded eyes, consider a darker skin-class swatch (alpha 204, so it still bruises) for the band in assets/source/palette/kicker.json, instead of plain slot 6.

votes.reason: The shipped config has the first build's z values that FIX-ART-A.md says it rejected. The 1 m crop shows the result: a blank pale band under the cap, with skin at the brim tips.
votes.evidence: In assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json the eyes region has max z 1.685 (line 434, min z 1.625) and the eyes zone has max z 1.69 (line 369, min z 1.62). FIX-ART-A.md:13 says the final values are region 1.625..1.665 and zone 1.62..1.675, and that 1.685 cut 2 cm off the cap's lower edge. A grep for '1.665' in the config finds nothing, and git history shows the same file (commit 94d0843). I compared r_kicker_f49_head.png before and after. Before, the eyes are a dark shaded band under the brim. After, the eyes are a flat pale skin band between the cap and the mask, and a skin-coloured lip sticks out at the cap's left tip. There are no shade features, so the face reads blank.
votes.root_cause: The first FIX-ART-A build (region max z 1.685, zone max z 1.69) was committed to pipeline.json, not the trimmed 1.665 / 1.675 values the call documents. The region recolours the cap's lower edge and brim underside to skin slot 6 instead of leaving them as cap. The plain skin swatch also has no darker shade for the eyes.

findings.title: InsetBlock recesses draw new ink seam lines on continuous walls, which break into dashes and crawl at distance
findings.detail: FIX-WORLD pulls an InsetBlock's drawn face back 2-4 cm over its whole extent. Many of those faces are only partly covered by the coplanar partner they were fighting: a wall end in a corner plane, a pillar between doors, the front walls beside the penthouse body. Where the partner's face ends, a 2-4 cm step now shows on what was a flush surface. The edge pass draws an ink line along it, full height or dashed. Seen in the tour, before|after: (a) roofs_catwalk, a new broken vertical line on the large brick wall; (b) roofs_terrace_doors, new outlines on the left edges and top of the brick pillars between the doors, in a fight arena at 3-6 m; (c) roofs_top_roof, a new vertical line on the right side face of the penthouse where PenthouseFrontWall1 (+x inset 0.02) meets PenthouseBody; (d) street_start, a pilaster whose ink line now runs its full height; (e) street_skyline_up, a dashed line parallel to a building corner. At the catwalk seam, per-frame change during the held pose rises slightly over BEFORE (0.95/0.65/0.57 vs 0.65/0.54/0.48 in the first frames), so the dashes crawl with the idle sway. The fixer checked only the gap, the deck and street A1/A2.
findings.evidence: tour/bot.avi (captures/m6-feedback-verify vs m6-feedback-review): f711 crop 400x420 at (1100,0), new dashed line at about x 1160, y 80-230 (pair2s.png); f555 crops at (330,120) and (1130,120) (pairs_b1.png); f815 crop 220x200 at (560,250) (pent_zoom.png); f45 crop at (1180,0) and f305 crop at (120,40) (pairs_c2.png); amplified difference of all 20 poses (tour_diff.png). Blocks: roofs.tscn Catwalk/EndWall0 (-x 0.02, partner RightAWall0 covers 22 of 30.2 m2), Terrace/RightAWall1 and RightAWallMid (-x 0.02), RightBWall2 (-x 0.04), TopRoof/PenthouseFrontWall0/1 (-x/+x 0.02, +z 0.02, +y 0.06), BackWall2 (+x 0.02); game/level/kit/inset_block.gd:28-34
findings.repro: Before|after at tour f711: ffmpeg -i <run>/tour/bot.avi -vf "select='eq(n,711)',crop=400:420:1100:0" for captures/m6-feedback-review and captures/m6-feedback-verify. Or in play, stand on the catwalk or the terrace and look at the long brick wall and the door pillars.
findings.suggested_fix: Only recess a face that its partner covers completely, so the recess stays hidden. Where neither face is fully covered (an end face in a corner plane, a pillar beside a door), stop sharing the plane in another way: shorten the drawn box along the axis where it overlaps the partner (pull the overlapping end back into the partner's volume), so no visible face is stepped. Extend tests/m6_coplanar_scan.gd to flag a recessed face whose area outside its partner is visible (a step of 0.005-0.05 m over at least 0.02 m2). Then re-record the tour and diff it against 82bab12.

votes.reason: Confirmed. tour f711 shows a new dashed vertical ink line on the brick wall in the verify recording and none in the BEFORE recording. It is a regression the wave introduced, not an approved departure or a logged call. The fix-world calls say the fixer checked only coplanar overlap, not the exposed step.
votes.evidence: I cropped tour/bot.avi frame 711 (400x420 at 1100,0) from captures/m6-feedback-review and captures/m6-feedback-verify. The BEFORE crop has a clean brick wall. The AFTER crop has a dashed dark vertical line at about x=62, y=80-230, on the wall left of the corner. roofs.tscn (game/level/mission1/) has Catwalk/EndWall0 as an InsetBlock with inset_min=(0.02,0,0), position (2.375,2.55,-7) and size (0.75,15.1,2). Its partner Terrace/RightAWall0 is a plain block (3,0.5,-7), size (2,11,2), which only partly covers the end face, so a 2 cm step shows where the partner ends. inset_block.gd _make_mesh shrinks the drawn box uniformly over the whole face, with no check that the partner covers it. tests/m6_coplanar_scan.gd (MIN_AREA_M2 0.02, _visible_area) only looks for faces still sharing a plane. It does not flag a recessed face that is partly exposed, so the regression passed the suite.
votes.root_cause: InsetBlock._make_mesh pulls the whole drawn face back by 2-4 cm. Where the coplanar partner covers only part of that face (corner-plane wall ends, pillars between doors, penthouse front walls), the remainder becomes a visible 2-4 cm step on a previously flush surface. The depth-and-normal edge pass inks that step, and the line breaks into dashes at distance and crawls with the camera sway. The scan checks only for shared planes, not for exposed steps.

findings.title: The hurt bearing uses the pitched view against the attacker's feet: beyond about 30 degrees of pitch, front and back swap
findings.detail: hit_bearing() takes local = view.basis.inverse() * (attacker.global_position - view.origin) with the camera's full basis, then atan2(local.x, -local.z). The attacker's origin is at floor level, 1.6 m below the lens. With the player looking down by more than atan(d/1.6) (29 degrees for an attacker 0.9 m away), an attacker directly behind lands in front of the camera plane. The bearing becomes 0: top strokes, no bottom strokes. Looking up by the same amount turns a frontal hit into 180 degrees (bottom strokes). Looking down that far is normal play: the ground moveset has a stomp and a stomp kick on downed enemies, so the player looks down while the rest of the crowd hits from behind. The FIX-FEEL tests use a level camera, so they cannot catch this. The roll is unaffected (its lateral component is the same); the overlay's top/bottom edge is wrong.
findings.evidence: game/camera/first_person_camera.gd:821-828 (hit_bearing). Hand calculation with the same maths: attacker behind at 0.9 m with pitch down 30/40/60 degrees gives bearing 0 (front); attacker in front at 0.9 m with pitch up 30 degrees or more gives 180. At pitch 10-20 degrees both are correct. The overlay passes camera.global_transform (hurt_overlay.gd:124-126), which includes pitch. game/combat/moves/stomp.tres, stomp_kick.tres, movesets/ground.tres exist.
findings.repro: Add a test to tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd. Pitch the player's camera 45 degrees down. Put a Punk 0.9 m behind and land a real jab through HitDetector. Assert that the bottom stroke weight exceeds the top. It fails today: edge_weights(0) lights the top.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the bearing in the horizontal plane. Take the view's yaw only: var fwd := -view.basis.z; fwd.y = 0; normalise it, with a fallback to view.basis.y when looking straight down. Project (attacker - lens) onto the XZ plane, then take atan2 of the components along right and fwd. Or build Basis(Vector3.UP, view.basis.get_euler().y) and use its inverse. Keep the -hit.direction fallback.

votes.reason: Confirmed by reading the code and hand-computing the maths. I did not run a Godot test. hit_bearing uses the full pitched view basis against the attacker's floor-level origin, so beyond about 30 degrees of pitch the bearing flips between front and back. It is an unapproved defect in new FIX-FEEL code, not a logged call or a spec departure. Medium severity is fair: a Punk behind the player while the player looks down to stomp gets the wrong overlay edge.
votes.evidence: game/camera/first_person_camera.gd:821-829 (hit_bearing): local = view.basis.inverse() * (attacker.global_position - view.origin), then atan2(local.x, -local.z). Hand calculation, pitch down 45 degrees, attacker directly behind at 0.9 m, lens 1.6 m up. Camera forward is (0, -0.707, -0.707) and the back axis (0, 0.707, 0.707). rel = (0, -1.6, 0.9) gives local.z = -1.6*0.707 + 0.9*0.707 = -0.495. That makes -local.z positive, so the bearing is 0 (ahead). The fallback does not rescue it: horizontal length sqrt(0^2 + 0.495^2) = 0.495, and hurt_bearing_min_m is 0.05 (tuning_data.gd:249). hurt_overlay.gd:105 passes camera.global_transform (pitch included, lines 124-126) to hit_bearing, and edge_weights lights the top edge for a bearing of 0. The roll is unaffected because it uses sin(bearing) and the lateral component is the same. Existing tests (tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd:489-520) use level views, so none of them catches it.
votes.root_cause: hit_bearing builds the local vector with the camera's full 3D basis, including pitch, and the attacker position is at foot level 1.6 m below the lens. The vertical offset therefore leaks into the forward/back component once the camera is pitched, and local.z changes sign. The bearing has to be measured in the horizontal plane (yaw only).

findings.title: The ground's z-mirror is visible down the street as a symmetric pair of grate, crack and patched square either side of the fold
findings.detail: The 16 m mirrored repeat replaced the 8 m one. Looking down the street, though, the drain grate, the branching crack and the outlined patched square appear twice, mirror images flanking the manhole row, within about 6-8 m of each other. The reflection reads as a deliberate symmetric layout rather than random ground. The brief asked that the 16 m mirrored repeat not be obvious. There is no seam or mip line at the fold.
findings.evidence: captures/m6-feedback-verify/drift/bot.avi f640 and f1100, crop 1000x200 at (300,380) (fold.png): the grate at about x 130-215 and x 240-290 and the crack-and-square at about x 500-700 near and mirrored far. Shader: game/fx/trim_body.gdshaderinc gtm = vec2(gt.x, abs(mod(gt.y, 2.0) - 1.0)).
findings.repro: Watch 'Look: ground drift' at A2 (f619-1218), or stand at street A2 and look down the street's length.
findings.suggested_fix: In tools/gen_trim.gd, keep the strongly shaped features (patched square, branching crack, grate) out of the half-tile next to the fold rows (v near 0 and 1), so a feature and its reflection are at least 8 m apart. Or make the patched square symmetric in z so its reflection looks like a second copy, not a mirror. Rerun gen_trim.gd --check and the A1/A2 drift numbers.

findings.title: Committed Kicker eyes config is the first build FIX-ART-A rejected, not the settled one in its calls file; the cap's lower edge reads short and the eyes are gone
findings.detail: FIX-ART-A A-4 says the first build (region z up to 1.685) cost the cap 2 cm of its lower edge, 'read short', and that 1.665 keeps the brim; the eyes zone is stated as z 1.62..1.675. The committed assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json has the `eyes` region max z 1.685 (min 1.625) and the `eyes` zone z 1.62..1.69. run.py --check reproduces the shipped GLB from this config, so the 1.685 build shipped. The new test box (z 1.63..1.66) cannot tell the two apart. In the fresh recording the cap's shadowed underside and thick brim of the BEFORE still are gone, the cap is a thin shell over a large bare forehead band, and nothing marks eyes.
findings.evidence: assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json (eyes region max z 1.685, eyes zone max z 1.69); docs/milestones/M6-calls/FIX-ART-A.md A-4 ('1.665 keeps the brim', 'z 1.62..1.675'); tests/test_m6_feedback_detail_kicker.gd:239 (box 1.63..1.66); captures/m6-feedback-verify/r_kicker/sheets/r_kicker/crops/r_kicker_f49_head.png against captures/m6-feedback-review/r_kicker/.../r_kicker_f49_head.png
findings.repro: cd the worktree; grep -n -A12 '"name": "eyes"' assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json; read the A-4 call; view the two head crops side by side.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide which numbers are the intended ones. Either set the region max z to 1.665 and the zone to 1.62..1.675 and rebuild (run.py --asset kicker, then --check), or correct the calls file and show a 1 m still of the shipped build. Tighten the test to pin the region's max z so the two builds differ.

votes.reason: The config/calls mismatch is real and reproduced by reading the files. The committed pipeline.json carries the build the fixer's own calls file says it rejected. I did not view the head crops (no image reads), so the "cap reads short, no eyes" visual claim rests on the reviewer's account plus the fixer's own note that 1.685 shortened the cap.
votes.evidence: assets/source/characters/kicker/pipeline.json: the eyes zone (slots 23,6) has min z 1.62 and max z 1.69. The eyes region (slot 6, only_from 23,6) has min z 1.625 and max z 1.685. FIX-ART-A.md A-4 states region z 1.625..1.665 and zone 1.62..1.675, and says "Region z up to 1.685 (my first build): the cap lost 2 cm of its lower edge and read short". The only commit touching the file after the ROLL-KICKER one is 94d0843 (the FIX-ART-A wip), so no later change reconciled the two. run.py --check said YES after the merge, so the shipped GLB is built from 1.685. tests/test_m6_feedback_detail_kicker.gd lines 238-240 use box z 1.63..1.66, and the 1.665 and 1.685 builds both pass it (the 1.685 build adds more slot-6 skin above 1.665). The test therefore cannot tell the builds apart. It also never pins the region's max z.
votes.root_cause: The fixer settled on 1.665 and 1.675 after seeing that 1.685 shortened the cap. The edit reverting to those values was never committed or never rebuilt. The calls file documents the settled numbers while the config and GLB hold the first build. The test box is too narrow, 1.63..1.66, to catch the difference.
files_to_change: assets/characters/kicker (the rebuilt GLB, via tools/pipeline/run.py --asset kicker, then --check)

findings.title: The Bruiser's per-clip strain ratchet was regenerated wholesale, loosening about 14 clips' `high` ceilings; the log names only `held` and one other clip
findings.detail: FIX-ART-B regenerated tests/fixtures/strain/bruiser.json after test_m4_done_when failed on `held`. The `whole` bars are unchanged, but about 40 clip rows moved. `high` rose on hold 3.505 -> 3.748 (+7%), hold_collar 4.238 -> 4.505 (+6%), bruiser_headbutt 4.214 -> 4.450, jump, thrown 6.455 -> 6.603, walk_* 2.997 -> 3.064, and more; `bad` counts moved (spine twist 179 -> 184). The cause is legitimate (the helmet and visor regions moved the colour-aware decimation borders, so the mesh changed), and `held` min 0.1489 -> 0.088 is explained. But the ratchet was reset for every clip rather than only `held`, and the log says 'a few other clips moved by noise both ways' without listing the rises.
findings.evidence: git diff 2afbe4d d582d21 -- tests/fixtures/strain/bruiser.json (python compare of old and new clips: held, hold, hold_collar, bruiser_headbutt, thrown, walk_* high up); docs/milestones/M6-calls/FIX-ART-B.md 'Ratchets moved'
findings.repro: git show 2afbe4d:tests/fixtures/strain/bruiser.json against the new file, clip by clip.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the regenerated `held` row and restore the old figure for every clip that only got worse (or list each rise with its figure in FIX-ART-B), or note that the whole-run bars (high_max 8.65) are the real bar and say so.

findings.title: The 'general' coplanar guard still leaves out the Dressing pieces and the crowd and training rooms' slivers
findings.detail: The brief asked that any two drawn faces sharing a plane fail. The scan keeps only LevelBlock meshes and world bodies; 83 Dressing ArrayMeshes (DressingStreet, DressingA, Roofs/Dressing, BossRoof/Dressing) are not boxes it sees. With Dressing meshes added to a scratch copy it reports 7 pairs: wall tops against cornice tops, all at y 11 (0.16-0.88 m2). They are high up and probably not seen from the player's heights, but the guard says nothing about them. The crowd room (17 pairs) and the training room (2) are held only to 0.5 m2 (ROOM_MIN_AREA_M2); real pairs of 0.02-0.3 m2 remain, including 0.29 m2 floor tops at y 0 and 0.25 m2 tops at 6 and 2.4. FIX-WORLD logs this as a request for the room builders.
findings.evidence: tests/m6_coplanar_scan.gd _box_owner (no Dressing case); scratch run with Dressing meshes: 'Geometry/RightWall2/Body and Street/DressingA1/CorniceR1: y+ face at 11.000, 0.16 m2' and six more; room probe at MIN_AREA 0.02: crowd 17 pairs, training 2; tests/test_m6_feedback_ground.gd ROOM_MIN_AREA_M2 0.5
findings.repro: Edit _box_owner to return the mesh for ArrayMesh instances under a node whose name begins with Dressing; run test_m6_feedback_ground.gd. For the rooms, call Scan.pairs(root, 0.02) on Snapshot.CROWD and Snapshot.TRAINING.
findings.suggested_fix: Inset the cornice tops by 2 cm (or drop their top face) and include Dressing meshes in the scan. Make the rooms' boxes InsetBlocks, or inset RoomKit.add_box, and drop ROOM_MIN_AREA_M2 to 0.02.

findings.title: INSET_STEP_M is a dead constant in InsetBlock; the insets are hand-typed numbers in 41 scene nodes
findings.detail: game/level/kit/inset_block.gd declares `const INSET_STEP_M := 0.02` and its doc says each tier is a step of it, but nothing reads it. The tiers (0.02, 0.04, 0.06 and per-axis mixes) are typed into the scenes, so the constant neither enforces nor documents anything checked, and a number sits in a script that CLAUDE.md's 'no numbers in scripts' rule would not allow if it did anything. Nothing validates that insets are tier multiples; only the scan catches a clash.
findings.evidence: game/level/kit/inset_block.gd:15; grep -rn INSET_STEP_M game tests tools finds only the declaration and a doc comment
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the constant and say '2 cm per tier' in the doc comment, or move it to an @export on a level-kit tuning resource and add a test that every inset is a multiple of it.

findings.title: The code-05 closure test is satisfied by a bare string, so a comment-only roll-out test file still opts its character out of the shared guards
findings.detail: _rolled_out(id) now needs the pipeline's detail_bake.crease, and test_every_roll_out_test_reads_its_own_pipeline_and_the_recipe asserts each tests/test_m6_feedback_detail_<id>.gd contains the text 'characters/<id>/pipeline.json'.
